product_name: 4 oz. Amber Boston Round Glass Bottle, 22mm 22-400 Black Child Resistant Calibrated Dropper
product_description: 4 fl. oz. (120 ml) amber glass boston round dropper bottle, 22 mm (22-400) neck finish, packaged with a calibrated black child resistant polypropylene (PP) plastic dropper and 108 mm glass pipette. The amber (brown) glass is able to filter out ultraviolet (UV) light and is primarily used for UV-sensitive products such as beer and some pharmaceuticals. This product also features calibrated markings to make measuring easier and more accurate. Boston rounds have a rounded shoulder and rounded base, making them popular in personal care packaging but also appropriate for applications in other industries. The dropper has a glass tube and rubber bulb ideal for dispensing essential oils, skincare and chemical products. These 4 oz. glass bottles are packed 128 bottles per case.
product_notes:
Products containing ethyl alcohol or pure essential oils may remove the printed graduation marks due to the liquid's corrosivity. Please test this dropper for compatibility with your product.
*It is recommended to clean before use.
Specific water-based calibration tests are conducted to meet standard measurements. As a result, this bulb dispenses up to 0.75ml of water-based product at a time.

product_materials.material_description: Material: Amber Glass - Made popular after the Civil War and now commonly known as the industry standard, the amber colored glass provides protection to light sensitive products such as hydrogen peroxide and sulfuric acid chemicals, along with beer, oils, skin care, and pharmaceutical drugs by blocking out UV rays. It has wavelengths shorter than 450 nm (nanometers), allowing it to absorb most ultraviolet radiation. Amber glass is a tinted glass produced by combining iron, sulfur, and carbon. Due to its high level of carbon, amber is referred to as a reduced glass. The Cary Company stocks popular amber glass containers such as Boston round and packer bottles. Discover if Amber Glass is appropriate for hot fill application by learning more about What Is Hot Fill Packaging and how it applies to Amber Glass containers.

product_materials.material_description: Material: Amber Glass - Made popular after the Civil War and now commonly known as the industry standard, the amber colored glass provides protection to light sensitive products such as hydrogen peroxide and sulfuric acid chemicals, along with beer, oils, skin care, and pharmaceutical drugs by blocking out UV rays. It has wavelengths shorter than 450 nm (nanometers), allowing it to absorb most ultraviolet radiation. Amber glass is a tinted glass produced by combining iron, sulfur, and carbon. Due to its high level of carbon, amber is referred to as a reduced glass. The Cary Company stocks popular amber glass containers such as Boston round and packer bottles.
